title: Psalm 137: By the Rivers of Babylon
summary: Exiles in Babylon remember how they sat by its rivers and wept for Zion, hanging up their harps when their captors demanded songs of joy. The singer swears never to forget Jerusalem, then turns to God with a cry for justice against Edom, which cheered Jerusalem's destruction, and against Babylon, ending with a blessing on whoever repays Babylon by dashing its infants against the rocks.

from.text: It belongs to a group of psalms often called imprecatory, meaning psalms that call down curses or judgment on enemies (others include Psalms 35, 69, 109, and 137).

line: Exiles in Babylon weep by its rivers and cannot sing the LORD's song; they swear never to forget Jerusalem and cry to God for justice, ending in the hardest lines in the Psalms.
guide: It honors grief and does not hurry the exiles to cheer up; you are allowed to hang up your harp for a while. If you carry rage at what was done to you or to someone you love, take it to God out loud instead of acting on it, and leave the judging to him. Its last lines are a prayer spoken to God, never a word to be turned against any people or any person.

care.text: One thing is not open. No reading of these psalms has ever made it right to harm anyone, least of all a child.

If you carry rage at what was done to you, or to someone you love, this psalm shows that God can hear even that. Your rage is heard. Hand it to God rather than to your own hands. Tell a trusted person: a pastor, a friend, a counsellor. If you are in danger, or fear you might hurt someone, get help today. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: Weeping by the rivers: how can we sing?
An oath never to forget Jerusalem
The cry for justice against Babylon

verses.t: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
There on the willows we hung our harps,
for there our captors requested a song; our tormentors demanded songs of joy: “Sing us a song of Zion.”
How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?
If I forget you, O Jerusalem, may my right hand cease to function.
May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem as my greatest joy!
Remember, O LORD, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell: “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”
O Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us.
Blessed is he who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.
